Geographic_Alignment: Both US municipal solid waste landfills experiencing elevated temperature reactions; ETLF is anonymized (5 sites), Bridgeton is explicit site in Missouri.
Temporal_Alignment: Disjoint time windows (ETLF: 2012-2019 periodic; Bridgeton: 2013-2019 dense daily/weekly).
Spatial_Resolution_Alignment: Point / wellhead gas sample resolution in both datasets.

Target_Variable_Feasibility: Gas & Temperature Reaction Hazard Risk Classification (Task C).
Risk_of_Mismatch_or_Leakage: Zero spatial leakage because sites are distinct; risk of model overfitting to Bridgeton well naming conventions if not stripped.
Evidence_and_Justification: Directly compatible in normalized chemical/thermal feature space. Both share wellhead temperature (deg C), CH4/CO2 ratio, and reaction risk indicators.

Geographic_Alignment: Exact facility match: Bridgeton Landfill is Landfill ID 1994 / GHGRP ID 1007341 in LMOP.

Evidence_and_Justification: LMOP provides waste in place (17M tons), open year (1952), closure year (2005), and gas system specs for Bridgeton.

Risk_of_Mismatch_or_Leakage: MODIS 1km-4km pixel footprint may capture surrounding agricultural or industrial fire. Requires type==2 (static land source) or high confidence filter.
Evidence_and_Justification: Essential spatial transformation: filters nationwide thermal anomalies down to verified solid waste dumpsite coordinates.

Geographic_Alignment: Completely disjoint: Bridgeton is an engineered US sanitary landfill in Missouri; Rajbandh is an open tropical dumpsite in Bangladesh.
Temporal_Alignment: Overlapping monitoring years (2013-2019), but sampling intervals differ (daily/weekly well sampling vs monthly site aggregation).
Spatial_Resolution_Alignment: Subsurface gas extraction wellhead (in-situ) vs 30m satellite pixel (Landsat) / site-wide monthly total.

Target_Variable_Feasibility: Comparative case studies of engineered reaction vs tropical open dumpsite warming.
Risk_of_Mismatch_or_Leakage: Mixing these datasets into a single training matrix would cause severe negative transfer and physical feature confusion.
Evidence_and_Justification: Serve as complementary standalone benchmarks: Bridgeton for subsurface chemical smoldering reactions; Rajbandh for tropical LST climatic coupling.

Geographic_Alignment: FFTA provides structural causal tree probabilities; Bridgeton provides empirical continuous sensor telemetry.
